question: In the beginner agents course, what's the difference between a global skill and a project-level skill?

question: How does Rob Snyder say to stop customers from churning right after they buy?
gold_answer: He says everyone who buys is guaranteed to churn until some milestone 'X', so you find the leading indicator after which churning would be weird (like a Slack team hitting a message-count threshold) and design onboarding as a 'bullet train' that gets every customer there. At his restaurant-software startup, getting a notification about a preventable quitter in the first two weeks after purchase was that milestone.
key_points: everyone churns until X; find the leading indicator of retention; Slack message count example; design onboarding to get every customer there
author: pm_proxy

question: What bounce rate did Sachin Puri say should worry a small business owner about their website?
gold_answer: He says if your bounce rate is more than 50%, meaning visitors open a page and leave without going to any other page, you should go and check right away. Losing half your visitors that way means you have a problem, which is why the hero image and tagline must make it clear they are in the right place.
key_points: bounce rate above 50%; check right away; clear hero image and tagline
author: pm_proxy

question: What LinkedIn acceptance rate does Rob Snyder say you should be hitting when you reach out to prospects?
gold_answer: If you send around 100 to 150 connection requests a week, he aims for 30 to 40 percent to accept, and then 30 to 50 percent of those should reply. If you are below that, your profile or your message is not interesting enough.
key_points: 30 to 40 percent accept; 30 to 50 percent reply; low rates mean profile or message is not interesting

question: How should I decide which niche or customer group to go after?

question: Do the guests think a human should still stay in the loop when AI agents do creative or design work?
gold_answer: Yes. The agent-harness guest says subjective work, where two people disagree on what good looks like, needs a human in the loop. The Grok Bot guest says never go straight to the output and that his own approval on design and functionality is necessary, because his feedback is what lets the AI work better.
key_points: subjective work needs a human in the loop; judgment calls; do not go straight to output; own approval on design and function

question: Should you show a demo on the very first sales call?
gold_answer: Jen Abel says no: for the first call, show no demo and no slides, just have a one-on-one dialogue for 30 minutes. Rob Snyder also makes it a 30 minute call and is iffy on a demo, since early on you probably have none, though later you might include a very short one.
key_points: no demo or slides on first call; 30 minute conversation; early stage may have no demo to show; maybe a very short demo later

question: What do the guests say about the security risks of letting AI agents run things for you?
gold_answer: In the beginner course the advice is to scope what the agent can access and limit tool permissions, for example read-only access to important platforms, so a compromised agent can't do much damage. The Grok Bot guest says to take the best model you have and run a /goal asking it to do security checks, and he also tests his apps with a guardrail-free 'obliterated' model.
key_points: scope what the agent can access; read-only permissions limit damage; run security checks with best model; obliterated model attack testing
author: pm_proxy

question: Where in the Josh Woodward episode does he warn against getting attached to the product idea itself?
gold_answer: At about 16:15 he says to think about the problem you are falling in love with, not the product, because it takes three, four or five pivots before you either have something or conclude it didn't work. Falling in love with the product solution first, in his experience, leads to a bad time.
key_points: fall in love with the problem not the product; three to five pivots
author: pm_proxy

question: When does Lenny ask Rob Snyder about Linear beating Jira, and what is Rob's take?
